caveats: Single-condition timing on an otherwise idle machine. Real campaigns additionally pay model loading, protocol resolution, result assembly and I/O per batch, and spot-instance retries.
A product of planning factors is not a measurement. Changing any one changes its total proportionally.
These are CPU-hours consumed: not vCPU-hours provisioned, not elapsed time, not money. See docs/computational_resources.md.

excluded_factors.per_donor_models: v10 states the plan informs a COMMON G1 model initialisation 'without fitting donor-specific models', so a donor multiplier is excluded from both columns.

model_revisions.basis: PLANNING ASSUMPTION: WP1 versions the model repeatedly before the WP2 freeze, and WP3/WP4 revise it again.

rate_sets.basis: PLANNING ASSUMPTION, and the weakest number here. v10 funds 'systematic sensitivity analyses' of rules, rates and initial conditions but states no ensemble size; current practice is 30.

scenarios.basis: MEASURED from the model: one variant per hypothesis family.

single_perturbations.basis: DERIVED: 32 internal (non-input) nodes, each forcible ON or OFF. v10 funds perturbation screening for intervention selection (WP4) and targeted perturbations testing selected dependencies before the WP2 freeze. It describes single perturbations, not combinations.

model_revisions.basis: PLANNING ASSUMPTION: WP1 versions the model repeatedly before the WP2 freeze, and WP3/WP4 revise it again.

pairwise_perturbations.basis: NOT FUNDED. 64*63/2 = 2016 unordered pairs. Combinatorial screening is a plausible future direction, especially for WP4 synergy, but no work package commits to it and no code here performs it.

rate_sets.basis: NOT FUNDED at this size: a full uncertainty-quantification target, against 30 in current practice.

scenarios.basis: MEASURED from the model: one variant per hypothesis family.

extrapolated.unit_basis: MEASURED: median CPU seconds for one 3-phase condition at 10,000 trajectories.
